Why is De-Ionized Water so special? Is it the same as Reverse Osmosis Water?

DI water is usually RO water that goes through an additional step of being run through ion exchange bottles (cation and anion) to pull out any dissolved elements. This leaves you with ultra pure water which is now not conductive, and somewhat aggressive as it wants to absorb things. Only useful for industrial or lab use, don't drink it or water plants with it.
What would happen if you drank it? Sickness or death I assume.

No, it just leaches minerals out of your body. it's not healthy, but trying a small amount won't hurt you. Just leaving it in a container it will absorb dust and some of the containers minerals, as soon as it hits your mouth it will absorb enough to stop being aggressive.
Ok...so it would only be dangerous if you tried replacing all the water you drank with DI water. Long term effects simply being various mineral deficiencies and possibly brittle bones?

Dangerous implies risk of danger, this is better called slow demineralization of your body and would damage it. It would strip minerals like magnesium ou t of the cells along your digestive tract first,and then your bones eventually. It's a really bad idea.

Thanks! Well, that answers the "Can I drink it?" question.

I know RO water goes through some rigorous filtration, but I now have the question of what is reverse osmosis?

K, here's how you make drinkable water.

Take whatever source of well water, run it through a course filter like sand (for high volume applications) or even just a typical course cartridge filter like Home Depot sells (10" is common). Then, run it though a very fine filter ( same as last one, but finer mesh) I like 1 micron. Run it through a carbon filter to grab an organic solvents or other odd things. Take your output of that and pump it through a RO set of membranes, RO membranes are like a thin sheet of fiberglass, crazy small pore sizes, this strips almost everything out but the tiniest dissolved minerals. Take the RO output and run it through a UV sterilizer as a precaution in case your RO has a pin hole in it, because while RO water is pure, things like viruses sneak through an imperfect filter and the uv sterilization kills everything biological. Drink, it will taste awesome. This is typical good bottled purified water, same as something like Dasani which is just pre-Coke before sugar and crap. Which makes one wonder why Coke is cheaper than Dasani since it's all the same, but Coke has more steps and more stuff in it...

To be honest, nothing much different that we have already. Most SCOTUS decisions are unanimous or lack dissents but have concurrences. Two of the three biggest legitimate constitutional issues in recent years were the individual mandate under the commerce clause (voted unconstitutional by a 7-2 margin though preserved under Congress's taxing authority) and the administration's unilateral expansion of EPA wetlands authority which were almost all overturned on a unanimous basis as running counter to property rights under the 5th amendment. The only decision that would have been different is Heller but even there, the then prevailing militia theory of the second amendment (i.e. right to bear arms was not an individual right) was only supported by 2 of the justices. The other 2 dissenting justices ascribed to a viewpoint that the second amendment was an individual right but it was still within the rights of the individual states to impose restrictive regulations on gun ownership. This theory definitely holds more intellectual rigor as not all rights under the Bill of Rights have been incorporated against the states. Heller simply incorporated the second amendment guarantees against the states.
